items.title: Inside Slayyyter’s Big Year: From ‘WOR$T GIRL’ Breakthrough to Best New Artist Grammy Nomination
items.summary:
When Slayyyter released her third album, WOR$T GIRL IN AMERICA , in March, she considered it to be her swan song. Her previous two albums, 2021’s Troubled Paradise and 2023’s Starfucker , hadn’t charted on the Billboard 200 , and the pop singer admitted in countless interviews that she believed her most recent effort would be her last .

Instead, the reaction was extraordinary. WOR$T GIRL IN AMERICA hit No. 22 on the Billboard 200 and No. 1 on Billboard ‘s Top Dance Albums chart. That success was enough to drive Slayyyter to a sold-out tour supporting her album (and the recent announcement that she’ll be headlining Madison Square Garden next June), but her big year didn’t end there. On Monday (Nov. 16), nominations for this year’s Grammys were announced, and Slayyyter received four nods: best new artist, best dance/electronic album, best dance pop recording for her song “DANCE…” and best dance/electronic recording for her song “CRANK.”

items.title: Executive Turntable: Melissa Victor-Burkhardt Joins HYBE Global Label Services
items.summary:
HYBE has appointed Melissa Victor-Burkhardt as executive vp of global artist services for HYBE Global Label Services. Within the newly created role, Victor-Burkhardt will work with the company’s worldwide teams to help with project management. She will also oversee a team of project managers for marketing, commerce, distribution, DSP and streaming.

Victor-Burkhardt previously served as senior vp, head of publicity and brand strategy at Epic Records, where she worked with clients including Future, Travis Scott, 21 Savage, Giveon, Mariah The Scientist, Madison Beer and Zara Larsson. She has also worked at labels including Interscope, J Records/Jive Records, Virgin, Island Def Jam and Bad Boy Records. 

“Melissa is a deeply experienced executive in the music industry who has worked across countless campaigns for global artists and has an acute understanding of the scope and teamwork required across both internal and external partners for demonstrated success,” Juan S. Arenas , president for HGLS, said in a statement. “She will work closely with our worldwide teams to strengthen and build an ecosystem that encourages services to HYBE IP, a continued collaborative approach, and a focus on high impact. I’m grateful to have her on board to help execute the vision of a globally built platform powered by best-in-class services.” 

Victor-Burkhardt added, “By helping artists grow from a first single to the global stage, my work has always been about strategically building careers that last. HYBE is redefining what a music company can be, and I’m excited to bring that experience to…
items.t: Executive Turntable: Melissa Victor-Burkhardt Joins HYBE Global Label Services

items.title: Every Track From ‘Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album’ Ranked
items.summary:
Monocultural moments in society have become extremely rare in the mid-2020s, but the arrival of Grand Theft Auto VI has brought about as strong a unified pop-culture tidal wave as we’ve seen this decade.

Rockstar Games released the Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album on Friday (Nov. 20) through Atlantic Records as an accompanying soundtrack to the long-awaited video game, which arrived 24 hours earlier. 

Rockstar didn’t spare any expense when piecing together the 34-track album, which features  Playboi Carti,   Dua Lipa,   Cardi B,   Lana Del Rey,  Gunna, Don Toliver, Kodak Black, Yung Lean, Future, Metro Boomin, Travis Scott, Fred again.., PinkPantheress, Morgan Wallen, Tame Impala, Fuerza Regida and more.

GTA VI will look to make even more history with a No. 1 debut on the charts — as no video game soundtrack has topped the Billboard 200 before.

Artist-hosted radio stations dominate the Vice City airwaves, with stations helmed or curated by the likes of Bad Bunny, Lana Del Rey, Morgan Wallen, Trina and Trick Daddy, PinkPantheress, Burna Boy and Robyn.

The Grand Theft Auto VI  festivities will continue into the weekend, with a music festival  at Miami’s Mana Wynwood on Nov. 21. The festival is set to have Cardi B, Travis Scott, Rauw Alejandro and more hit the stage, including a Cactus Jack ensemble featuring Scott, Don Toliver, SoFaygo and a cameo from Florida’s own Kodak Black.

Take a break from perusing Leonida with Jason and Lucia and find all 34 tracks from Grand Theft Auto: The Album ranked in order below.
items.t: Every Track From ‘Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album’ Ranked

items.title: Music Venue Trust and Fender team up for intimate London showcase gig with Unpeople
items.summary:
The Music Venue Trust and Fender have teamed up for an intimate London showcase gig with up and coming Bristol band Unpeople.

The venture entitled The One. For London. aims to support London’s grassroots music scene kicking off with a concert at the dive bar Blondies in Hackney on December 1. Tickets are available to purchase here and all fans in attendance will receive a Limited Edition Fender The One. For London. t-shirt on the night.

“We all started out in small venues just like Blondies,” said Unpeople. “So it feels very special to team up with Fender and get to play a show like this, for a cause that’s very close to our hearts. Support small venues that give bands like ours a place to start. We are unpeople, you are unpeople, we are all unpeople.”

Liam Cunnah, Executive Vice President, EMEA, Fender, added: “The One. For London. is about giving back to the grassroots music venues that make Fender possible and supporting Music Venue Trust’s ongoing efforts to protect these vital spaces,” said Liam Cunnah, Executive Vice President, EMEA, Fender.

“These venues are the beating heart of the UK’s music culture, providing a platform for emerging artists to find their sound and connect with audiences. Through The One. For All. and the American Professional series, we’re celebrating the connection between artists, the instruments they play and the stages that give them a place to be heard.”

The event marks the next chapter in Fender’s collaboration with MVT, which began with a nationwide call for fans to nominate their favourite grassroots venues to win Fender gear in…
items.t: Music Venue Trust and Fender team up for intimate London showcase gig with Unpeople

items.title: Harvey Mason, Rufus Reid & More Are Named 2027 NEA Jazz Masters: Full List
items.summary:
Harvey Mason has watched his son Harvey Mason Jr. become CEO of the Recording Academy and one of the most visible people in the music field. But jazz fans know Mason Sr. as a celebrated drummer, composer and producer in this own right. And now he’s a Jazz Master, so declared by The National Endowment for the Arts.

Related 

John Legend, Janelle Monáe & More Among Performers Slated for Inaugural L.A. Jazz Festival

The Jazz Masters Fellowship is the nation’s highest honor in jazz. The Arts Endowment, in collaboration with the DC Jazz Festival, will honor this year’s five recipients in a tribute concert on Monday, April 5, at Arena Stage in Washington, D.C., and streamed online.

Here’s a look at this year’s five honorees:

Terry Gibbs , 102, is a vibraphonist, bandleader and composer. Over the course of his long career, he recorded more than 80 albums, composed more than 300 works and led the Dream Band. 

John Edward Hasse , 78, is a scholar, writer and pianist. Hasse is the recipient of the 2027 A.B. Spellman NEA Jazz Masters Fellowship for Jazz Advocacy. He is also a two-time Grammy nominee, for best historical album and best album notes, both in 1989 for The Classic Hoagy Carmichael . Hasse is the founder of the Smithsonian Jazz Masterworks Orchestra and Jazz Appreciation Month.  

Harvey Mason , 79, is a drummer, composer and producer. Mason is a 10-time Grammy nominee, counting both solo work and his role in the group Fourplay.…

“You’re catching these characters at a totally different part of their life,” Brennan told Variety in an interview published Thursday (Nov. 19). “The timing of these characters thinking, ‘Maybe that was the best time in my life, being in that choir in high school’ and then once you think that you’re like, ‘Oh, that show’s going to work.’”

items.summary:
Billie Eilish will headline BST’s Hyde Park festival in 2027, joining the London festival’s stacked slate for next summer.

Related 

Harry Styles, Sam Fender & Billie Eilish to Headline Glastonbury Festival 2027: See The Lineup 

Billie Eilish & FINNEAS Follow Lucy Dickins to CAA for Global Touring, WME to Share in North America 

Harry Styles Hits Festivals & Billie Eilish is Back: The Biggest Talking Points From Glastonbury’s 2027 Lineup Reveal 

Eilish will headline the iconic venue on July 3, 2027, her first time performing at the festival. The announcement comes just days after she was revealed as one of Glastonbury’s headline artists in 2027. She first topped the festival bill in 2022, becoming the youngest solo act to ever do so.

She now joins Bon Jovi , Muse and RAYE as performers on the BST Hyde Park lineup for 2027, with more due to be announced in the coming weeks. Support acts for Eilish’s performance have not yet been shared.

Tickets for the performance go on presale from 3 p.m. GMT on Friday (Nov. 20) from the festival’s website , with a general sale commencing on Thursday, Nov. 26, at 10 a.m. local.

From New York via Montana
Recommended if you like Cameron Winter, Tobias Jesso Jr, Alex G
Up next Supporting Caroline on tour in Canada and the US until 19 November

Isaac Eiger is something of a scene legend in the world of American indie-rock. Raised in Bozeman, Montana, he was the founder and lead singer of the cult shoegaze-adjacent six-piece Strange Ranger, who left heartbroken a small, fervent fanbase when they announced their breakup in 2023. Taking a discernibly British approach to their sound, Strange Ranger traversed C86-y jangle-pop before landing on Madchester rave-up for their final album, 2023’s Pure Music. But Eiger is nothing if not musically worldly: he has written and produced with both underground heroes (Cassandra Jenkins, Chanel Beads) and nascent pop stars (Adéla, Frost Children).

Ever-prolific, Eiger also has a solo project under the name Threshold, with which he released a gauzy, 19-minute EP in 2024 called Thief. Earlier this year, he released Stillwater, the first single from the debut Threshold album, due for release in 2027 on the London-based label Untitled. Although Stillwater has some clear influences – it owes some phrasings and intonations to Alex G, but what indie-rock song doesn’t these days? – it’s still a remarkable song: expansive and…

items.title: The month’s best experimental album: Stella Z’s ambient adventures into lucid dreaming
items.summary:
(CDR)
Based around sounds recorded on her trips back to China, the Fujian-born, London-based producer creates a curious nocturnal collage on Thunder Is the Sky Dreaming

Lucid dreaming is one of the influences behind Thunder Is the Sky Dreaming, the new record from Fujian-born, London-based producer Stella Z. “Every night is an adventure,” she writes in the liner notes, “I can even smell things in certain dreams.” The eight tracks here are suitably sensory, scattered with effervescent sounds, ephemeral whispers and polyrhythmic percussion.

Many of the sounds and textures were recorded during trips back to China – the ambient noises of a pharmacy or the Fujian mountains late at night – a curious, collage-like approach that underpins the record. On The Somnium Is Awaiting My Cue, we hear what appear to be insects buzzing around a plodding bassline and sporadic woodwind motifs, while electronics softly spiral. Similarly hypnotic is Mira Miruna, on which the echoes of words gradually reveal themselves among the fizzing, softly discordant arrangement: a warped, increasingly urgent call to “wake up”, reminiscent of the foggy state as you rise from sleep. Z amplifies this heady feeling later on in Exit, Elsewhere, where her overlapping narration and rattling bells cause total disorientation.

Continue reading...
items.t: The month’s best experimental album: Stella Z’s ambient adventures into lucid dreaming

Listening to Wonderkids, the string-laden opener of Take That’s new album, it seems the three remaining fiftysomething boybanders are feeling reflective. “Forgiving you, forgiving me / This vicious circle is now complete,” sings Gary Barlow.

In the years since their last record, the band – and former member Robbie Williams – have indeed laid out the trials and tribulations of 35 years of Take That in several documentaries, some more candid than others. Earlier this year, they even embarked on a revival of their blockbuster 2009 Circus tour. Unfortunately, all this reminiscing has left their 10th album feeling so steeped in nostalgia that any moments of greatness struggle for attention.

items.title: ‘We’re the most arrogant of all apes!’ A delightfully mind-expanding encounter with Peter Gabriel
items.summary:
From sampling to streaming, the rock legend has always been in thrall to technology – but is superintelligence a step too far? Back with an epic new album, he unpacks his remarkable ideas

Peter Gabriel asks me to fetch my laptop: he wants to show me a video of himself playing a keyboard duet with a bonobo called Kanzi. In fairness, said footage is, as Gabriel suggests, “extraordinary”. Working with primatologist Sue Savage-Rumbaugh, who developed a means of communicating with bonobos involving sign language and a speech-synthesis keyboard, Gabriel plays droning chords on a synthesiser while Kanzi picks out complementary notes on a piano. “Look, she likes that note, which is a ninth, and then she finds the octave,” he enthuses as the video plays. “There’s a real musicality there.”

It is all deeply unlikely, but it seems the perfect illustration of how easily a conversation with Gabriel can go wildly – if fascinatingly – off-piste. I’ve only been in his company for 10 minutes, long enough to ask a solitary question about his epic new album o\i: its 13 tracks last nearly 90 minutes, the result, he suggests, of a longstanding interest in African music “which made me realise that a song could last as long as a song could last”, and of “being old enough to think ‘fuck it’, really”. For anyone who feels that an hour and a half of exquisitely arranged, beautifully produced, occasionally deeply strange art rock – its sound shapeshifting from the folk-flecked A Hard Lesson to the glowing pop hues of Till Your Mind Is Shining – is too meagre an offering, it arrives in…
items.t: ‘We will become cyborgs!’ Peter Gabriel on bonobo ape duets, building a Jurassic Park for plants – and why AI will make great music

items.title: Jeff Buckley was a 90s indie darling. Now gen Z think he’s the ‘yearner final boss’
items.summary:
With his unguarded lyricism and earnest delivery, the late singer-songwriter is having a moment among a generation that fetishizes unrequited desire

Sydney Tripoli has collected Jeff Buckley memorabilia since 2019. She keeps her collection of T-shirts, posters, vinyl and other merch celebrating the late singer-songwriter in what she affectionately calls her “Buckley box”. The 27-year-old scours eBay and resale sites for these pieces; lately she’s noticed the prices “skyrocket”.

“During the pandemic, it was impossible to find Jeff Buckley shirts. Now they’re everywhere on Depop,” said Tripoli, who works as an actor in Los Angeles. “Now [my collection] is worth thousands of dollars.”

items.title: Nothing compares to her: Sinéad O’Connor’s 20 best songs – ranked!
items.summary:
The Irish singer-songwriter would have turned 60 in early December. To mark the occasion, we revisit the best of a catalogue that’s far more than a certain Prince cover

This suitably uncompromising opener to the lengthy Faith and Courage offers a collage of radio static, Indian-inspired beats, dub bassline and whispered vocals. More importantly, it’s fantastic: you might call it trip-hop were Sinéad O’Connor’s vocal not so intense as to negate any potential for relaxation on the part of the listener.

items.title: Is Lorenzo Senni’s All Ages the year’s wildest electronic album?
items.summary:
(Warp)
The Milan producer revisits his youth as a straight-edge punk fan voyeuristically dabbling in rave – and finds a thrilling interzone between both genres

The opening line of the biography on Lorenzo Senni’s Bandcamp page is striking. “Lorenzo Senni was never a raver,” it reads, something of a blunt admission from a dance producer, or at least a producer who works in an area of electronica influenced by dance music: one might reasonably assume you need some first-hand experience of the dancefloor’s ineffable freedom in order to make music for it. But the Milan-based Senni has made a USP out of his arm’s length distance from what that Bandcamp bio calls a “neon-hued chemical world”.

A straight-edge punk fan in the late 90s, he accompanied friends to Rimini’s hardcore and gabber clubs as a kind of anthropological exercise, a self-styled “rave voyeur” who “just liked to observe and analyse my surroundings”. Accordingly, his albums to date have dealt in what approving critics like to call deconstructions or interrogations of dance music rather than dance music itself: 2012’s Quantum Jelly and 2014’s Superimpositions featured what Senni called “pointillistic trance”, spinning the icy, staccato notes and arpeggiated synth lines of the genre’s epic breakdowns into lengthy, beatless tracks that never reached the climax implied. items.title: ‘I have to sell my bum on OnlyFans to go on tour’: Kate Nash on fame, feminism and fighting the music business
items.summary:
She threw a (metaphorical) brick through Spotify’s window and exposed industry failings with her ‘Butts for Tour Buses’ campaign. Now the singer is embracing her Irish roots with her new album’s fighting spirit

Kate Nash was standing on a fire truck in a showgirl outfit complete with white tights and pink G-string, shouting through a loudhailer about the music industry’s failure to pay artists fairly, when she wondered if she’d gone too far. It was 2024 and the truck, which made pit stops outside the London offices of Spotify and Live Nation, had a large black-and-white picture of Nash’s bum on the back along with the words “Butts for Tour Buses” – a reference to her newly launched OnlyFans account, which she was using to fund her tour.

That afternoon, she called her manager Kat. “I told her: ‘I’ve thrown a brick through the window at Spotify.’ She went: ‘What, literally?’ and I said: ‘No, but I’ve been standing outside their offices with a megaphone, so that relationship is over. I don’t think we’ll be making their New Music Friday feature.’ And we didn’t.” [see footnote]
